The zero-subspace base case has singleton identity compact representatives. Actual logarithm membership implies the logarithm is zero, and the proved genuine exponential/logarithm inverse shows every subgroup element is the identity. The proved genuine lattice-reduction step gives a unit-interval real parameter, an element in the next admissible coordinate-zero slice and an original lattice integer power. The next compact representative set is multiplied on the left by the actual compact unit-parameter exponential segment. The target is an existential compact set contained in the genuine subgroup with proved right representatives for every subgroup element. No compact quotient, compact section or fundamental-domain assumption is a premise, and the theorem is not restricted to commuting Lie subalgebras.

To pass to the genuine restricted-lattice coset quotient, the actual ambient compact set is lifted by the natural subgroup subtype embedding. The proved subset-of-range property gives compactness of this preimage. Each original lattice right factor is also proved to belong to the subgroup by x^{-1}g, using subgroup membership of the two actual factors. The retained original lattice closedness and actual quotient inclusion theorem prove a closed embedding and compact ambient orbit. Its real extension is therefore rational for that original lattice structure.
